body.content:
Hi Alex,

  

Thank you again for completing the exterior stair work and helping us obtain
the final Certificate of Occupancy on November 3.

  

I am asking you to reconsider our earlier request and extend the current Base
Rent abatement for aleast three additional months, covering December 1, 2026
through February 28, 2027, with Base Rent commencing April 1, 2027. We would
continue paying NNN, utilities and other applicable Additional Rent during
this period.

  

The fire alarm work took approximately 142 days - April-to-August. During
substantial portions of this period, critical-path tenant work—including
closure of the affected ceilings and progress toward final inspections—was
materially delayed.

  

We have made a substantial investment in the premises and incurred significant
carrying costs while being unable to operate. A three to four month extension
would help the new business stabilize after these construction and compliance
delays while preserving the long-term landlord-tenant relationship.

  

Please reconsider allowing Base Rent to commence on April 1, 2027. We would
document the revised commencement date in a short written lease amendment
before December 1.

  

Thank you for considering this request. I would be happy to discuss it with
you directly.

  

Best regards,

Bharath

Smash District, LLC

body.content:
Hi Bharath,

Thank you for your response. Carney remains committed to completing the
outstanding items within our contractual scope and bringing this project to a
satisfactory close.

I want to clarify our position regarding the outstanding balance of $52,184.44
and the applicable provisions of our agreement.

The project has received its Certificate of Occupancy, iSMASH Everett is open
and operating, and Carney has issued its Certificate of Substantial Completion
establishing November 5, 2026, as the date of Substantial Completion. We have
also issued our written one-year warranty dated November 18, 2026.

Section 9.1 establishes payment of the remaining 10% of the contract price
upon issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy. That milestone has been
reached.

We acknowledge Sections 9.1.7 and 9.1.12, which provide for withholding 150%
of Carney's estimated cost to complete agreed unfinished items. We are
prepared to reconcile those items in accordance with the agreement. However,
these provisions do not expressly require independent subcontractor quotations
or disclosure of internal vendor pricing as a condition of payment.

**1\. Punch List and Remaining Work**

Carney has already provided the updated punch list.

The Smash Room 3 door has been ordered and is scheduled for installation the
week of November 30, 2026. The paint room door levers will be replaced during
the same visit.

Regarding the fan switches, Carney will issue a $300 credit toward your
outstanding invoice to resolve this item.

**2\. HVAC**

Carney completed the balancing of the operational HVAC unit. The second unit
was not functioning at the time of balancing and therefore could not be
balanced.

As the nonoperational unit was subsequently repaired by your vendor, that
vendor will need to perform the balancing associated with its repair.

Carney has already performed the balancing work possible under the conditions
present at the time. We do not agree that additional balancing of the
previously inoperable unit, following repairs performed by others, falls
within Carney's remaining contractual obligations.

The previously supplied HVAC balancing report documents the work completed.

**3\. Substantial Completion, Warranties and Closeout Documentation**

Carney has issued its Certificate of Substantial Completion, effective
November 5, 2026, together with its written one-year warranty.

We will coordinate delivery of any remaining applicable equipment manuals and
inspection or testing documentation required by Sections 3.8.3 and 3.8.4. We
are also available to arrange a joint closeout review.

**4\. Change Order Documentation**

This project was contracted on a lump sum basis. The approved change orders
and contract reconciliation establish the adjustments to the contract price.

Carney is not obligated under the agreement to disclose its internal
subcontractor invoices, vendor pricing, or proprietary cost information.

The request for individual subcontractor quotations, detailed labor and
material breakdowns, vendor contacts, and internal invoices is excessive and
unnecessary to determine the cost of completing the remaining agreed punch
list items.

We will provide the reasonable completion-cost estimate contemplated by
Sections 9.1.7 and 9.1.12, but we will not produce internal subcontractor
invoices or require our vendors to prepare additional quotations solely to
support withholding payment.

**5\. Subcontractor Payments and Lien Waivers**

All subcontractors have been paid in full. The consolidated closeout package
includes the applicable subcontractor lien waivers, Onesta's unconditional
waiver, Carney's conditional waiver, and the contract payment reconciliation.

**Final Payment**

After applying the $300 credit for the fan switches, the outstanding invoice
balance will be $51,884.44, subject to any separately agreed adjustment under
the contract.

Section 9.1.2 provides for payment of undisputed amounts even where portions
of a payment application are rejected.

We propose that the parties promptly reconcile any remaining unfinished
contractual items, agree upon Carney's estimated completion costs and
reasonable completion dates, and apply any withholding in accordance with
Sections 9.1.7 and 9.1.12.

The remaining punch list should not serve as a basis for withholding the
entire outstanding balance when the agreement provides a specific mechanism
for addressing unfinished work.

Please confirm your availability for a joint review and identify any specific
objections to the Substantial Completion documentation so that we can address
them directly.

Carney will continue coordinating the remaining agreed work. We request prompt
payment of the undisputed portion of the outstanding balance in accordance
with our signed agreement.

Regards,

Troy Fink

Client Relations
